Thunderbird stores user data by default in a profile within the %appdata% area of a Windows user account and ~/.mozilla within a *nix user home folder which as far as I know can be backed up with a manual copy/paste at the easiest, or scripted with your favourite sync utility (rsync, robocopy, etc) or backup program.

This Mozilla page might be of some additional assistance.
Is your email account a pop3 or imap account?

If you are running Win7 or later you will need the script "take ownership". Install it then use File Explorer, go to documents & settings, "owner", then to local settings, to application data, thunderbird, profiles, profile name. At each step up to and including profile name you will right click and see "take ownership" as an option. Run it each time. This will allow you to unblock each folder and files therein so you can see each of them. Copy the Profiles folder to your backup device. It will contain your mail folders with all email therein. I have a 15 year archive of email saved this way. I store my TBird profile on an external usb-powered hard drive to save space on my laptop SSD then back it up to the same drive plus a duplicate to a 128gb USB memory stick. As for saved attachments I have not had an opportunity to see if this is done but I do not see why not.
